sugyot.title_en: the mishnah: one who spread a sheet beneath the sekhakh because of the falling leaves -- pasul
if he spread a sheet over it (the sekhakh) because of the sun, it is unfit
if one trained a vine, a gourd or ivy over [the sukkah] and roofed on top of it -- pasul

the mishnah: whatever is not susceptible to impurity and whose growth is from the ground -- one may roof with it

R' Yochanan (via Rabba bar bar Chana): roofing with hushnei of flax -- I do not know its status. Left open; the text records no תיקו.
one may roof [the sukkah] with boards -- R' Yehuda
one who roofs his sukkah with skewers or with the long boards of the bed: if there is space between them equal to them, it is valid

the mishnah's clause: [one who roofed it with skewers] or with the long boards of the bed -- [unfit roofing]
the mishnah: one who hollows out a grain stack to make himself a sukkah -- it is not a sukkah

'ohel'-'ohel' from the Tabernacle (Bamidbar 19:14 / Shemot 40:19): as the Tabernacle's tent is made by man, so the tent of corpse-impurity -- stated by the stam as R' Yehuda's source (יליף)
one who sleeps under the bed in the sukkah has not fulfilled his obligation

one who supports his sukkah on the legs of a bed -- it is valid

the mishnah: a sukkah whose shade exceeds its sun is valid

one who makes his sukkah between the trees, and the trees are its walls -- it is valid

those on a mitzvah errand are exempt from the sukkah
